title: Chapter 191: Did I Forget to Put on Make-up Today?
html:
The security guard has carried the actor inside the box out?

Standing in the autopsy-room doorway, Chen Ge looked back along the corridor. His eyes narrowed. Darkness had little effect on him. I didn’t hear them dragging anyone away. They must be hiding.

When he closed the autopsy-room door, flakes of rust fell from its frame. The equipment throughout Tian Teng Medical School looked genuinely old. Rubbing the rust between his fingers, Chen Ge examined the room’s instruments. This isn’t artificial aging. They must have taken these directly from an abandoned hospital.

To achieve authenticity, some Haunted Houses bought obsolete equipment cheaply in bulk, refurbished it, and incorporated it into their sets. The operating table and electrocardiograph here were examples.

A code hidden behind the machine confirmed it: 2-2-1-15. Hospitals used such markings to track and categorize equipment, identifying the department, equipment type, maintenance classification, and individual unit. Exact systems varied, but the principle remained similar.

Lingering spirits usually attach themselves to whatever is nearby when they die. If all these props came from a real hospital, perhaps this place truly is haunted.

Chen Ge was merely speculating. After all, he had no evidence. Of course, this might just be another trick by Tian Teng Medical School.

Another room opened off the autopsy room, filled with hanging white sheets whose purpose Chen Ge could not discern. Uninterested in exploring it, he continued down the dim corridor, only to find a steel door secured by a massive lock.

Looks like I’ll need the key before I can move on.

With the route ahead blocked and the autopsy room already searched, his only option was to return to the chamber of white sheets.

Bloodstained sheets hung from the ceiling, making the chamber resemble a crime scene. Pushing through the heavy fabric, Chen Ge entered an even darker and more disturbing space. The organs and limbs missing from the autopsy-room mannequins lay scattered here among several severed mannequin heads.

Now this isn’t bad.As the attraction’s first visitor, Chen Ge found the fake blood still wet enough to cling unpleasantly to his shoes. This room connects to the autopsy room, and the security footage mentioned an illegal organ trade. This must be where it happened.

Tian Teng Medical School’s Japanese design team pursued visual horror with an intensity local creators rarely matched. Approaching the heap of organs and severed limbs, Chen Ge noticed something curious.

The female mannequin on the operating table was missing its heart. The others lacked organs too, but none so important. I haven’t seen a heart anywhere. Could the key be hidden inside it?

Where would the heart be?

An idea occurred to Chen Ge as he surveyed the abandoned organs and limbs. He bent to search the pile. As he lowered himself, a human head concealed among the props suddenly opened its eyes and screamed.

Scars covered the face, and tears of blood streamed from its eyes. Hair clung to its neck. The figure began to rise, sending organs and limbs rolling aside, but made it only halfway before a hand pressed firmly on her skull.

“Shh. Be quiet.” Chen Ge pushed the “ghost” back into her hiding place. His enhanced vision made the dark almost as clear as daylight, and he had noticed the slightly unnatural head the moment he entered.

The heap concealed a petite young woman among the fake organs. Pinned in place by Chen Ge, she had no idea how to respond. Nothing like this had ever happened, and the employee handbook certainly offered no instructions for it.

She sat back down. With Chen Ge’s powerful hand resting on her head, she completely forgot her lines.

“Heart, heart… where are you?” People said a serious man was the most attractive, but as the “female ghost” watched Chen Ge sift through fake organs while murmuring about a heart, she shivered.

“Found it.” He opened a model heart hidden behind her and discovered an exquisitely made key. Taking it, he left at once, abandoning the bewildered “ghost.”

She watched him go, trying and failing several times to speak. Once he was gone, she rearranged the props and resumed her position. “Did I forget to put on makeup today?”

Beyond the locked door, the atmosphere became more sinister. Tian Teng Medical School’s limited floor space had encouraged meticulous design, with scares packed closely together.

Green lights flickered after he passed through the steel door, and white sheets lining the corridor fluttered in an artificial wind.

The corridor is half a meter narrower. Something must be hidden behind the walls.Chen Ge knocked on the surface. I was right. The wall on the left is hollow.

A few steps farther, he reached the third room, which was filled with cribs containing infant mannequins.

A nursery?Chen Ge surveyed it from the doorway. The instant he crossed the threshold, the cries of children filled the room. “All right, don’t cry. Come to Uncle. Now, where are you hiding?”

Multiple speakers made the crying seem to come from every direction.

Every room here serves a purpose. The autopsy room hinted at the heart; the chamber of white sheets hid it; and the heart contained the key. This nursery should hold something I need as well.

In the center of the room, something tugged his shirt. He turned to find an infant mannequin reaching from its crib and clutching the fabric. Its face was discolored as though poisoned, with remarkably detailed makeup.

The arm has no articulated joint, so it must be hollow. There should be a control wire somewhere.Chen Ge looked around. To grab me at precisely the right moment, the operator has to be nearby. They must be hiding under the crib.
